To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Chipman Lake complex is a 1.1 Ga alkaline complex that formed in a rift-related environment, and the Seabrooks Lake complex is a younger 0.8 Ga alkaline intrusion that formed in a post-rift environment.
The Chipman Lake and the Seabrooks Lake carbonatite complex are of Keweenawan age, and the Chipman Lake is a carbonatite dike swarm, whereas the Sebrooks Lake is a carbonatic syenite complex.
the Chipman Lake complex was emplaced during the late Keweenawan, at about 1098 Ma, in the Wabigon Subprovince of the Canadian Shield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the paleomagnetism and geochronology of the Keweenaw Peninsula, Michigan, and the Keweenawan carbonatite complexes of the Superior and Abitibi subprovinces, Ontario.
the petrogenesis of the Seabrooks Lake carbonatite complex in the Abitbi Subprovinces, Ontario, Canada, and the Chipman Lake carbonatite in the Wabigon Subprovinces.
the paleomagnetic analysis of the Keweenawa carbonatite complexes of Chipman Lake and Sea brook Lake, Ontario.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Keweenawan age pole position of the Chipman Lake complex is 186°E, 38°N (dp = 7°, dm = 11°), corresponding to an age of 1099 ± 10 Ma, and the Keweenawan Seabrook age pole position is 186°E 38°N (dm = 8°, dp = 10°), corresponding to a Keweenawa age of 1101 ± 10  Ma
the Seabrooks Lake complex was intruded in the early Keweenawan at 1118 ± 8 Ma.
the Chipman Lake carbonatite complex is 1098 Ma old, whereas the Sebrook Lake alkalic syenocarbonatite stock is 1085 Ma old.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that both the Seabrock Lake and Chipman Lake complexes have primary remanence and are Keweenawan in age.
both complexes were formed at 1098 Ma and that their host rocks were deformed at 1098–1060 Ma.
the Keweenawan age for the Chipman Lake Complex is 1098 Ma ± 10, which is the same as the age obtained from K–Ar ages of amphiboles from the fenite.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chipman Lake complex was emplaced during the Keweenawan, which is in agreement with previous K–Ar and Rb–Sr studies.
the Seabrooke and Chipman Lake complexes are both of Keweenawan age and were formed during the same time interval.
